I1.quote: High-pressure (0–80 bar) H2 adsorption/desorption isotherms were recorded at 77 and 298 K using a SETARAM Hy-Energy PCTPro-2000 manometric system and ultra-pure (99.999%) H2 gas.

I2.quote: The polymer-derived activated carbon (denoted hereafter as PDAC) was produced by carbonization and chemical activation procedures using PANi as a carbon precursor.

I3.quote: An excess gravimetric H2 uptake of ~5.5 wt% at 77 K and ~58 bar was recorded for the PDAC
I3.location: main, p. 6, Section 3.3 (H2 storage performance); also Table 3, p. 7

I4.quote: The PDAC exhibits a SSA of ~2193 m2/g and a SPV of ~1 cm3/g, whereas the YP80F reference has a slightly lower SSA and a slightly higher SPV (i.e. ~1889 m2/g and ~1.1 cm3/g, respectively).
I4.location: main, p. 5, Section 3.2 (Structural characteristics); values in Table 1 (SDFT, QSDFT from Ar at 87 K)

I5.quote: The development and in-depth characterization of multifunctional materials with versatile use in energy and environmental applications has been a topic of on-going investigations.

notes: Two carbon sorbents measured: KOH-activated polyaniline-derived carbon (PDAC) and commercial activated carbon YP80F (Kuraray). H2 uptake measured volumetrically (manometric PCTPro-2000, 0-80 bar, 77 and 298 K; low-pressure 0-1 bar at 77, 90, 100 K on the Autosorb). The electrochemistry in the paper is supercapacitor ion electrosorption in 1 M CsCl, not hydrogen storage, so it does not trigger the electrochemical code. Surface areas are QSDFT (Ar, 87 K) and SAXS-derived; no BET value. Table 3 defines Cg (wt%) as mH2/(mH2+msolid), i.e. W2, and also gives Cn in mmol/g. Synthesis is cited to ref. [29], but the paper does not state that its H2 uptake values were published before. No retraction notice; record is_retracted false. No supplementary files were provided.
